title: Realign a drifted repository to its declared participation, then converge to a no-op
description: The walking-skeleton outcome for bootstrap-as-reconciliation. A repository declares its intended participation; the alignment command computes the difference against what is actually true -- in the repository, in the tool environment, and in per-host state outside any checkout -- reports it as a delta, applies it, and on a second run changes nothing. Its subject is repository participation: something the platform owes a repository, not a bar the repository must clear. Written to fail: nothing implements this today. vuoro-bootstrap is the initiation half only (one-shot external onboarding for Vuoro Cloud, release-gated), and no command performs the routine-realignment or schema-migration halves the plan names.

inputs.request: Given a repository whose declared participation and actual state disagree, report every difference as a delta, converge the repository to the declaration, and prove the run is idempotent.
drift_cases_that_must_be_detected: A documented setup instruction that is wrong: AGENTS.md directs `sprintctl[remote]`, but the served transport lives in the `served` extra. Following the documented rule leaves `vuoro_client` missing and every served command fails with an unrelated ImportError.
An absent virtualenv: the Makefile falls back to the system python when `.venv` is missing, so the failure surfaces as `No module named ruff` rather than as missing setup.
Uninstalled JS dependencies: no target installs `apps/web/frontend` node_modules, so the failure surfaces as `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND openapi-typescript`.
Per-host state outside every checkout: Playwright browsers cached under `~/.cache/ms-playwright`, which no repository can carry.
A missing participation field: no `authority_repo_uuid` in the dispatch manifest, so every sprintctl authority command is refused client-side.
Guidance that instructs a removed command: five repositories' `item-done` skill directed `sprintctl item done-from-claim`, deleted from sprintctl by 0.3.4.
A silently wrong work authority: a repository with no `.sprintctl/backend.json` resolves `backend=local` and writes work nobody can see, while appearing to succeed.
deliberately_not_assumed: that the repository was ever correctly bootstrapped
that drift is confined to the repository working tree
that a declared instruction is a correct instruction

metadata.subject: repository participation
metadata.note: Written to fail, before anything is built. Every drift case above was measured on 2026-08-29, not imagined: five during the §10 item 6 loop run (recorded as workflow.friction ad:01M16CWY219TYRG3023J7EEA55, ad:01M16DP9D58G1855F7Z7K25HKF, ad:01M16DV0EJ81MAVF1B5QEGV2ZY, ad:01M16E57Y784QVQNR1TJ4SJRQH, ad:01M16F0PAW8C4832C17ZPJT37J), one found by a skills sync diff, and one inherited from the cred-broker incident of 2026-08-28.
metadata.why_this_subject: Plan §2 records that consumer integration is an admission subject carried by no surviving scenario. This is not that scenario, but it is the half that must exist first: a consumer cannot be admitted against a participation nothing can verify.

facts: drift: reported as a declared-versus-actual delta, naming the facet
drift: a documented instruction that no longer works is reported as drift, not propagated
drift: state outside the repository is compared, not assumed
dry-run: diff produced with no file, tool, or credential mutated
apply: actual state matches the declaration for every selected facet
idempotence: a second run reports converged and changes nothing
exit code: non-zero while unconverged, so drift is detectable in CI without parsing output
migration: a repository pinned to an older participation schema realigns by rerunning, not by hand-editing
credentials: referenced by location, never copied into the repository
work authority: a repository resolving to an undeclared backend is drift, not a successful run
evidence: each alignment run emits an auditctl event carrying the delta it found
